authority: Severity reflects what a failure actually costs. HARD_FAIL blocks the release. STRONG_WARNING and SOFT_WARNING report and do not block. Unclassified checks default to STRONG_WARNING so an unreviewed check cannot silently gate a release.

severity_definitions.HARD_FAIL: Blocks the release. Money, secrets, legal exposure, or structural integrity of published pages.
severity_definitions.STRONG_WARNING: Reported prominently, does not block. Quality and hygiene.

post_deploy_checks.reason: Everything in `validators` runs against the repo or a local `next start`, so nothing in this gate can see what the edge actually serves. This check fetches the live hosts and therefore cannot be a pre-merge gate: on a pull request the fix under review is not deployed yet, and gating the merge on production state would red every PR that fixes production. It runs once per deploy instead, from the workflow named here. validate:registry asserts the lane is not inert - the npm script exists and the workflow invokes it - so it cannot become a script nothing runs. Rule 8 (31 Oct 2026) is the reason stated plainly: PR #51 fixed the Clarity loader at source and added a build-time gate for it, both green, and then the Workers Builds deploy of that commit failed, so all four hosts went on serving a <link rel="preload"> and no executable script while the fix sat in main and Search Readiness e6/i8 went on failing. This lane now asserts, per host, that the declared checkout page serves its conversion form and an ENABLED Clarity script and that the loader the edge hands back carries that host's own project id, and it fails on zero conversion pages reached.

validators.reason: five published Kindle EPUBs print these five paths on their last page. The link is baked into files that are already built, so a broken path here cannot be fixed by editing this repo - the remedy is re-uploading five books. Nothing else in the gate ties an app route to an external published artifact, and route_ownership.json alone cannot fail when both the route and its expectation are deleted together, which is why the five paths are hardcoded in the validator.

validators.reason: Five published Kindle EPUBs print https://weddingpdfchecklist.com/amazon/<slug> on their last page. That hostname transposes the canonical one and is baked into files already on sale, so a host-level failure - no DNS, an invalid certificate, or the redirect losing the path - cannot be fixed by editing this repo and breaks every reader arriving from a book. validate:amazon-paths covers the five paths on the canonical host and cannot see the host the books actually print. This gate fetches all five over HTTPS on the book domain, requires a 301 to the same path on weddingchecklistpdf.com ending in a 200, and separately asserts the alias is never declared as a canonical host - a second host that renders would be a duplicate indexable copy of the whole site. It uses the canonical host as a network control so an offline machine reports UNPROVEN rather than a false red.
validators.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-29: the gate exited 1 with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on all five printed URLs before weddingpdfchecklist.com was attached to the Worker, and passed once attach-book-domain.mjs created the custom domain and the deployed middleware answered 301 -> 200 on each path

Bing Webmaster and the site audit of 2026-09-25 read these off the rendered pages: rules 113/117 on weddingseatingchartmaker.com/products/seating-chart-maker (the http:// copy answered 200 beside the https:// one on all four hosts), rule 118 on descriptions of 81-98 characters with 25 more past 160, and 94 internal links (21-27 /free-wedding-planner?... per product host, 22 /products/*, /guides/* and hub links on weddingchecklistpdf.com) that 308'd across hosts. Rule 6 added 31 Oct 2026 (Search Readiness e6/i8 and e9): a rendered page with a conversion form must run the Clarity loader as an enabled <script>, and a page without one must not reference it. ConversionAnalytics used next/script `afterInteractive`, which injects the tag from the client after hydration, so every form and buy page on all four hosts served only a <link rel="preload"> - which executes nothing - and the first seconds of every session went unrecorded. validators.reason: a repair that exits non-zero, or exits 0 having changed no file, must never be recorded as a repair. validators.reason: full-safe-autonomy.yml ran the self-heal reporter as `node -e "..."`, and one line of the embedded JavaScript wrapped an interpolated repair_command in backticks. Inside a double-quoted shell word a backtick is command substitution, so bash executed `'+cmd+'` before node saw the script: run 33863160216 (main, 2026-09-04) logged "+cmd+: command not found", the failed substitution expanded to the empty string, and the job summary printed "repair_command is not runnable:" with the command deleted from the end of it. The step still exited 0 - the repo's recurring runs-but-inert class, a diagnostic that survives and silently drops the one fact it exists to carry. This scans every inline interpreter invocation in every workflow for unescaped ` and $ using double-quote semantics, and first proves the scanner works by running it over a table of known-bad and known-good bodies including the exact line from that run, so a corpus containing no inline scripts still cannot pass by having found nothing to look at. Counts detector cases, workflow files and run blocks, and hard-fails on zero of any of them.
validators.manual_repair: move the embedded script into a file under scripts/ and call it from the workflow - that removes the shell from the path entirely and makes the logic testable. Escaping the offending character as \` or \$ also works but leaves the next edit exposed.
validators.repair_evidence: proved negatively on 2026-09-05: restoring the original inline block in full-safe-autonomy.yml fails with "full-safe-autonomy.yml:153: unescaped ` inside an inline `node -e \"` script - command substitution", quoting the offending line; pointing the validator at a tree with an empty .github/workflows fails with "no workflow files", at a tree with no .github/workflows at all with "there is nothing to scan", and at a workflow with no run: blocks with "zero run: blocks were found". Restored, it passes with 8 detector cases, 5 workflow files, 47 run blocks and 1 inline script. Behavioural proof of the fix: run against the self-heal report fixture, the old inline step emitted "repair_command is not runnable:" with an empty tail, the file-based step emits "repair_command is not runnable: `fix the route's link`".

validators.reason: Full Safe Autonomy run 34957914196 (main, 2026-09-15) passed every gate, committed 7f8bbfd in its last step, and its bare `git push` came back `cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at 7f8bbfd7... but expected fd94a6fb...` - the sha the server was 'at' is the commit the step had just made. The update had been applied; the response said it had not; the receipts were on main and the run was red. A bare push takes a rejection as final without asking where the ref actually is, and is equally blind to the ordinary race where another lane lands between rebase and push. All three lanes that commit from CI (full-safe-autonomy, search-intelligence, self-heal) now push through scripts/ci/push_back.sh: fetch, PUSH_ALREADY_LANDED when the ref already contains HEAD, otherwise rebase and bounded retry, PUSH_REBASE_CONFLICT (red, nothing forced) only on a genuine conflict. This validator first proves the script against throwaway bare repositories - apply-then-reject, concurrent push, genuine conflict, nothing to push - and proves that the old bare push FAILS under the first, then requires every workflow that runs `git commit` to invoke push_back.sh with no bare `git push` and no --force. Counts scenarios, workflow files and commit-and-push lanes, and hard-fails on zero of any of them.
validators.manual_repair: replace the bare `git pull --rebase ... && git push ...` in the named workflow with `scripts/ci/push_back.sh "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`. If the failure is PUSH_REBASE_CONFLICT on a run, the lane's commit and a human commit edited the same lines: rebase by hand, never with --force.
validators.repair_evidence: proved negatively on 2026-09-15: with the three lanes still on a bare push it fails with 7 findings naming full-safe-autonomy.yml:212 and :234, search-intelligence.yml:52 and self-heal.yml:121 plus 'never invokes scripts/ci/push_back.sh' for each; against a copy of the tree with an empty .github/workflows it fails with 'no workflow files'; against workflows that never commit it fails with 'examined zero lanes'. Reproduced the run's shape locally against a bare repo whose pre-receive hook applies the update then declines: the old step exits 1 with the commit already on main; push_back.sh exits 0 as PUSH_ALREADY_LANDED. Restored, it passes with 5 behaviour scenarios, 5 workflow files and 3 lanes.

repair_contract: Two fields, and the difference is load-bearing. `repair_command` is EXECUTED verbatim by scripts/selfheal/heal_until_clean.mjs on failure, so it must be a real command: an npm script that exists in package.json, or a node script whose file exists. `manual_repair` is prose for a human and is never executed - it is printed by the loop and named in the job summary. Putting prose in repair_command is what broke the daily authority lane: the loop shelled out "add the route's label to lib/site-directory.ts (or a hub/landing record) ...", bash died on the unbalanced quote in "route's" with exit 2, and the loop burned all three attempts calling that a failed repair instead of reporting NO_REPAIR_AVAILABLE with the instruction a human could act on. Eight of thirteen repair_commands were prose. scripts/validators/validate_repair_contract.mjs now enforces this split. A validator may declare repair_command only when that command fixes the same defect this validator detects; pairing a repair with a validator it does not actually fix would turn the self-heal loop into a way of making failures disappear, so an unpaired validator is the correct and honest default.

scheduled_checks.reason: Fetches every sameAs and profiles_pending URL in data/seo/entity.json weekly. Network state cannot gate a merge, so it runs on a schedule: dead profiles (404/410) leave sameAs and pending profiles that now resolve are promoted, through a PR; a profile that resolves without linking back is a NAMED STOP naming the exact field the owner edits; JS-rendered platforms are recorded unverifiable, never passed. Its decisions are unit-tested inside validate:entity-graph.

Daily 05:55 America/Chicago: reads the brands Buffer (sent posts, 28 days) and Cloudflare Web Analytics (Instagram/TikTok referred visits to weddingchecklistpdf.com, 28 days) and commits data/brand-social/metrics.json for the scorecard. Network state cannot gate a merge, so it runs on a schedule; Cloudflare unreadable is a NAMED STOP and a red run, a metric it cannot measure is absent with an unread reason, never 0.
